request.prompt:
Make a new scene-state reference by precisely editing the approved courtyard in IMAGE 1. Keep its ORIGINAL short stone passage scale and location, high side walls, rock rear wall, broad empty earthen yard and sole SOUTH human doorway at lower-left. IMAGE 2 only specifies stone details; do NOT enlarge the passage to its close-up scale. IMAGE 3 gives long timber, IMAGE 4 gives the knife, IMAGE 5 gives the old lamp. One scene, morning diffuse daylight, 16:9.
State: third-day preparation, ropes reinforced and worn cloth pads installed; knife west, lamp beside the doorway with walking route clear. No people, drum, snake or invented tool piles.
At the NORTH gate, put ONE continuous long timber in FRONT of both posts. Bind it ONLY to ONE short cleat on the moving gate panel using TWO compact reinforced rope bands, BOTH entirely within the two posts. Neither fixed post has any rope around it. The bare upper through-post locking rod remains inserted and untouched; gate fully closed at this preparation moment. Put small clearly visible pale worn cloth pads under the two central reinforced binding/contact areas to protect rough edges. No third rope binding, no fixed-post tie, no long dangling ropes. Maintain space between long beam and low stone covers, and original compact stone body continuous into rock.
Knife: one thick-backed single-edged grey blade from image 4 lying flat on a LOW stone to WEST/left of the passage. Its wood handle and two dark wraps match the original; no second blade, no upright knife.
Lamp: open the unique foreground-left human door. The lamp from image 5 stands on the ground INSIDE THE YARD, just to the RIGHT of the doorway, pressed against the INNER SOUTH WALL surface. It is OUTSIDE the rectangular doorway opening and NOT between the two door jambs. Leave the doorway floor and route through its centre completely EMPTY. A slightly higher view can show the lamp behind the foreground wall; lower lamp partly occluded by wall is acceptable, moving it into the doorway is not. Keep pale patched paper, bamboo ribs and arched handle.
Same restrained hand-painted linework and muted earth/grey palette, original compact passage. All required objects belong to this same environment, no inset or montage. Highest native output.
